published_statement: HV 0802.0658 p.7-8: 'This theory can be formally derived as the leading 1/N approximation of quantum gravity interacting with N independent and identical free quantum fields ... By keeping the value of N G finite ... the gravitational field can be treated as a c-number field ... Let (M, g_ab) be a globally hyperbolic four-dimensional spacetime ... [T^R_ab = T_ab + F^C_ab I, (3.6)] ... for any pair of physically acceptable states, i.e., Hadamard states ..., the matrix element <psi|T^R_ab|phi> ... is finite and satisfies Wald's axioms. ... The choice of these counterterms is not unique but this ambiguity can be absorbed into the renormalized coupling constants which appear in the equations of motion for the gravitational field. The semiclassical Einstein equation for the metric g_ab can then be written as G_ab[g] + Lambda g_ab - 2(alpha A_ab + beta B_ab)[g] = 8 pi G <T^R_ab[g]>, (3.7) ... both the stress tensor and the quantum state are functionals of the metric ... The parameters G, Lambda, alpha and beta are the renormalized coupling constants, respectively, the gravitational constant, the cosmological constant and two dimensionless coupling constants which are zero in the classical Einstein equation.' HV p.13 (3.3): 'the scope and limits of semiclassical gravity are not well understood ... the semiclassical theory should break down when the quantum fluctuations of the stress tensor are large.' HPS p.3: 'In the realm of semiclassical gravity, one sets the Einstein tensor equal to the expectation value of the stress-energy tensor operator of the quantized fields present: G_mu nu = 8 pi <T_mu nu>. (1)'; p.4: 'G^nu_mu(f(l), r(l)) = 8 pi <T^nu_mu(f(l), r(l); xi)>, (3)'; fn [20]: 'We have also set the scalar mass and temperature to zero: m = kappa = 0. In this case, the arbitrary renormalization scale parameter mu appearing in (T^nu_mu)_log can be absorbed into the definition of f.' FW p.2: 'G_ab[g_cd] = 8 pi <T_ab[g_cd]>, (1.1)'; p.1 'we modify the perturbed semiclassical equations by the "reduction of order" procedure to eliminate spurious solutions. We also restrict attention to the limit in which the lengthscales determined by the state and metric are much larger than the Planck length'; p.3 '(1.1) contains time derivatives of order higher than two ... runaway solutions ... in general there are still open questions with respect to the extraction of physical predictions from the semiclassical equations'; p.2 'violations of ANEC in semiclassical gravity may be confined to the Planck scale, where the semiclassical approximation itself is suspect.'
published_hypotheses: S1 (HV 3.1) leading 1/N approximation: N identical free fields interacting only with gravity, N G held finite; gravity a c-number (tree-level) field.

S3 (HV 3.1) <T^R_ab> renormalized by local counterterms, in a Hadamard state, satisfying Wald's axioms; the counterterm ambiguity is ABSORBED INTO renormalized couplings G, Lambda, alpha, beta -- so the equation is a FAMILY (3.7), and G_ab = 8 pi <T_ab> is its member Lambda = alpha = beta = 0 (HPS eq. (1), FW eq. (1.1)).
S4 (HV 3.1) state and metric solved together (both functionals of g).
S5 (HV 3.3; Kuo-Ford) validity requires stress-tensor fluctuations small relative to the mean; scope 'not well understood'.

S6 (FW Sec. I) higher-derivative equation with spurious/runaway solutions; physical predictions need a prescription (reduction of order, established only for perturbation theory about flat space); lengthscales >> Planck length.

S7 (HPS) hbar = c = G = 1, MTW signs (fn [19]); one conformally coupled scalar xi = 1/6, m = kappa = 0; <T> in the Anderson-Hiscock-Samuel approximation; renormalization scale mu absorbed into f (fn [20]).

lacked_data: What HPS (1996) and FW (1996) lacked: (i) Lambda -- measured since (1998; Planck 2018 2.846e-122 l_P^-2); computed irrelevant at the throat (ratio 1.7e-125, C8a): having it changes nothing. (ii) The renormalized quadratic-curvature couplings alpha, beta that HV (3.7) makes free and that G = 8 pi <T> sets to zero -- STILL lacked: the only bound read (Calmet-Hsu-Reeb 2008, c2 < 1e61 at mu ~ 1e-3 eV) is 1.7e66 times larger than the b at which HPS's throat disappears (C8b), and the log running to the Planck scale is not measured. Having a measured beta WOULD change the throat conclusions: r0^2 = -16 K^2 L - 2b, and the sign of <rho + p_l> on the throat flips with the sign of b (C6). So M's hypothesis is CONFIRMED in a precise sense for this result -- the authors lacked a datum and the conclusion depends on it -- but the datum is lacked by everyone, not superseded: the equation is not shown inaccurate, it is shown to be one member of a family whose member is chosen by an unmeasured coupling. Evidence against M's stronger reading: nothing measured since 1996 contradicts the equation or HPS's b = 0 algebra; every tree figure is reproduced exactly (C4c, C5a-b, C6a-b). Data that would test the equation as a fundamental law (Page-Geilker 1981, NAMED-NOT-READ; the superposition proposals of 2605.24103) concern macroscopic superpositions, not vacuum-polarization back-reaction, and are not used by the tree.
